title: Microdramas Emerge as India's Fastest-Growing Entertainment Format
excerpt: A Meta-Ormax study reveals that 89% of viewers discover microdramas through social feeds, as the category scales to a projected ₹2,320 crore market by 2028 with major platforms and Bollywood studios racing to enter the space.
body:
• 89% of Indian viewers discover microdramas through social media feeds rather than active search, according to a Meta-Ormax Media study
  • India's microdrama market was valued at ₹650 crore in 2025, projected to grow over 50% annually to reach ₹2,320 crore by 2028
  • Over 60 million users actively watch microdramas monthly on ShareChat and Moj alone, generating approximately 650 million daily episodic views
  • Major studios including Yash Raj Films and Red Chillies Entertainment are evaluating entry into the microdrama space in 2026

From Reels to Serialized Stories

Microdramas — short, serialized stories told in 60-to-180-second episodes, designed for vertical smartphone viewing — have rapidly emerged as a distinct content category in India's digital entertainment landscape. What began as a social media curiosity has become one of the country's fastest-growing media segments, attracting Bollywood studios, major streaming platforms, and corporate advertisers.

A study by Meta and Ormax Media, titled "Micro Dramas: The India Story," found that 65% of viewers discovered the format within the past year. The research, conducted between November 2025 and January 2026 across 2,000 personal interviews and 50 in-depth interviews with audiences aged 18-44 across 14 states, paints a picture of a category building habits from scratch.

Feed-First Discovery Changes Everything

The most significant finding: 89% of viewers encounter microdramas through social media feeds, not through active search. This represents a fundamental shift in how entertainment content is distributed and consumed in India.

"Microdrama isn't a passing trend — it's rewriting the rules of Indian entertainment. In under a year, an entirely new category of platforms has emerged, built audience habits from scratch, and created a business vertical that is scaling fast."

— Shweta Bajpai, Director, Media & Entertainment (India), Meta

Unlike traditional OTT formats designed for long viewing sessions, microdramas are built for "in-between moments" — commutes, work breaks, and late-night scrolling. Viewers spend a median of 3.5 hours per week watching across 7-8 short sessions daily, with peak consumption between 8 PM and midnight. Around 90% of viewing happens solo, making it one of the most personal formats in India's digital ecosystem.

A Crowded and Growing Ecosystem

The microdrama space in India is already packed with major players. JioHotstar's Tadka, ZEE5's Bullet, Amazon MX Player's Fatafat, and Tata Play's Shots are competing alongside independent platforms like Kuku TV, QuickTV, and StoryTV.

ShareChat's QuickTV has reached 50 million downloads and 3.5 million paying subscribers, supported by a catalogue of more than 500 original series. The broader ecosystem counts over 200 million active monthly users, with over 60 million actively watching microdramas each month.

The FICCI-EY Media & Entertainment Report valued India's microdrama market at ₹650 crore in 2025, projecting it to grow over 50% annually to reach ₹2,320 crore by 2028. India accounted for 11% of global microdrama app downloads in Q1 2025 alone.

Bollywood and Brands Move In

The format's commercial potential has drawn attention from India's biggest entertainment houses. Yash Raj Films, through its streaming arm YRF Entertainment, and Shah Rukh Khan's Red Chillies Entertainment are independently evaluating entries into the microdrama space in 2026.

Corporate brands are following suit. Companies including Mahindra Finance are using microdramas for storytelling campaigns, finding that the episodic format builds narrative continuity and higher recall than traditional advertising. Tier-II and Tier-III markets account for over 75% of consumption, giving brands access to a young, heartland demographic — over 70% of viewers are male, with roughly 80% in the 18-34 age bracket.

"Micro dramas are beginning to show the early signs of becoming a distinct content category in India's digital entertainment landscape. When a format aligns closely with how audiences naturally engage with their devices, it has the potential to scale very quickly."

— Shailesh Kapoor, Founder & CEO, Ormax Media

The Economics Advantage

Production costs for microdramas run between ₹20,000-25,000 per minute, translating to ₹12-15 lakh for an hour-long series — a 70-90% cost reduction compared to mainstream television or OTT production. This low barrier is fueling rapid content creation, with platforms racing to launch new shows daily.

The biggest remaining challenge is monetization. Only 28% of viewers have ever paid for microdrama content, with a median preferred price point of Rs 75 per month. Platforms are experimenting with freemium models, micropayments per episode, subscription packs, and advertising-led revenue. Regional language expansion — with Tamil, Telugu, and Kannada seeing strong traction after Hindi and English — is also driving deeper market penetration.
